question.problem:
Given that the log-likelihood function for a particular sample of independent Bernoulli random variables is

$$
l(\theta )=5\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ),
$$

what is the maximum likelihood estimate $\overset{^}{\,\theta \,}$ from this sample?
question.worked_solution:
In order to find the maximum likelihood estimate of $\theta ,$ we calculate the derivative of the log-likelihood function, set the derivative equal to zero, and solve for $\theta .$

First, we take the derivative of $l(\theta ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}l}{\text{d}\theta } & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(5\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta )) \\  & =\frac{5}{\theta }+\frac{1}{1-\theta }\cdot (-1) \\  & =\frac{5}{\theta }+\frac{1}{\theta -1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we set the derivative equal to $0$ and solve for $\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{\theta }+\frac{1}{\theta -1} & =0 \\ \frac{5(\theta -1)+\theta }{\theta (\theta -1)} & =0 \\ 5(\theta -1)+\theta  & =0 \\ 6\theta -5 & =0 \\ 6\theta  & =5 \\ \theta  & =\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, for this sample, the maximum likelihood estimate of $\theta $ is $\overset{^}{\,\theta \,}=\frac{5}{6}.$
